subject: Clarify operator-auth model, DPA annex and transient cross-region handoff window
messages:
From: Olivia Park <ops-legal@omnihealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@omnihealth.com
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify operator-auth model, DPA annex and transient cross-region handoff window

Aditya,

Thanks for taking this — a few items we need clarified before Procurement will move forward with the DPA annex and procurement checklist:

1) Operator authorization: our security team prefers a customer-controlled operator pattern (customer-managed role / operator account) so that no Redwood-managed operator credentials are required to perform failover for private deployments. Is that model supported for Private (VPC / on‑prem) and Dedicated? If not, what controls are available (e.g., signed operator actions, audit-only operator keys)?

2) Cross-region transient processing: Exhibit B references emergency failover but doesn’t have a timebound window. For our regulator we need a clear maximum transient processing window for cross-region hops (we typically accept up to 72 hours if telemetry and audit evidence is provided). Can Redwood commit to a maximum window (hours) and provide the telemetry/audit evidence type you will provide?

3) Subprocessors: please send the active subprocessor roster for EU and APAC and confirm whether any analytics/telemetry vendors will process plaintext request payloads in other regions during a failover window.

4) KMS / key escrow: we need to understand KMS model for Private vs Hosted. Do you support customer‑managed keys (BYOK/HSM)? If not, is escrow available for legal hold / audit?

We attached our standard DPA annex request for reference. If possible can you provide a short one‑pager we can circulate to our InfoSec and Legal outlining operator auth options and the evidence you’ll provide for transient processing (logs, KV cache traces, request IDs)?

If it helps, happy to do a 30m call — procurement and legal are around this week.

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Legal Ops, OmniHealth
[attachment: OmniHealth_DPA_Annex_Request.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <ops-legal@omnihealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify operator-auth model, DPA annex and transient cross-region handoff window

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, full details below and attachments.

1) Operator authorization: For Redwood Private (VPC / on‑prem) we support a customer‑managed operator model. Customers can create a scoped operator role/account that we can perform runbooked actions against (we never persist the customer operator credentials in the control plane). For Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools) we support a delegated operator model with strict RBAC and signed action logs; we can discuss adding a customer operator role for enterprise deals (we have one recent customer running this configuration).

2) Transient window: Standard platform SLAs allow ephemeral failover but we usually commit to a 48h transient processing window for Hosted → fallback paths. For enterprise DPA annexes we can accept an explicit up to 72h window provided all of the following are fulfilled: (a) pre-authorized failover policy, (b) full request/response audit logs retained for 90 days, (c) KV cache/attachable prefix telemetry (request ids, timestamps), and (d) immediate notification to the customer with automated trace links. We attach our proposed runbook + evidence checklist.

3) Subprocessors: attached is a snapshot (redwood_subprocessors_snapshot_20270221.csv) showing subprocessors by region today. Short summary: analytics vendor (DeltaMetrics) receives anonymized telemetry only and is geo‑bounded; no vendor processes plaintext in other regions during normal ops. During emergency failover, control-plane telemetry may transit to our US telemetry ingest for processing; we’ll provide log extracts on request as part of the evidence package.

4) KMS: Private supports customer BYOK (Cloud KMS/HSM) with split-key options. Hosted supports customer-managed keys for Dedicated tenants (we bind keys to tenant IDs). For Hosted public tiers we use Redwood-managed keys by default but we can offer key‑wrap escrow for enterprise addenda.

Next steps: I’ve attached the runbook + evidence checklist and a short summary one‑pager. Can we schedule a 30m call Tue/Wed to run through the proposed AnnexB redline? I’ll loop Marissa (legal) and Markus (security) who can answer the redline and ops/telemetry details.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachments: redwood_subprocessors_snapshot_20270221.csv (csv); Redwood_operator_auth_runbook_20270221.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <ops-legal@omnihealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify operator-auth model, DPA annex and transient cross-region handoff window

Olivia / Aditya — looping in our legal redline. Quick clarifications from Legal:

- Exhibit B redline: we propose explicit language that permits transient cross‑region processing for resilience for up to 72 hours when (i) the failover event is documented in our incident system, (ii) the customer has pre‑approved the failover policy in the control plane, and (iii) Redwood provides an evidence package (request ids, timestamps, a signed incident summary) within 14 days.

- Operator auth clause: we will add a paragraph that confirms customer‑managed operator roles are available for Private and can be extended to Dedicated under a SC‑SLA. The paragraph calls out that operator actions are logged, signed and retained for 1 year.

- KMS addendum: we can offer BYOK/HSM for Private and Dedicated with a limited escrow workflow for legal hold. Escrow requires an MSA addendum and is subject to an access request process (audit, court orders, etc.).

Attached: DPA_AnnexB_redline_20270222.docx (proposed redline). Aditya, can you confirm the telemetry artifacts we’ll provide (formats and retention) so I can map them to the redline? Markus — please confirm we can produce the request id / KV cache traces on the timeline above.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: DPA_AnnexB_redline_20270222.docx (docx)]

Subject: Re: Clarify operator-auth model, DPA annex and transient cross-region handoff window

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what we need. A few quick notes:

• OmniHealth is comfortable with the proposed 72h window if the evidence package is automated and includes request ids, server timestamps, and a signed incident summary.
• For Private deployments we will require customer‑managed operator roles + BYOK; for Dedicated customers we are open to SC‑SLA binding for operator auth.
• Please provide the DocuSign link for the DPA annex redline (we’ll have Legal + Procurement sign). Our procurement contact is procurement@omnihealth.com — procurement will also request the HubSpot deal reference (OMNI-4312) in the DocuSign message.

We’ll schedule the 30m call once the DocuSign/redline is up. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Legal Ops, OmniHealth
